title: March in Zhangjiajie - the mountains awaken
text: Temperatures of +8 to +16 C, nights still chilly. Frequent fog is great for photographers. Big pluses: minimum tourists, lowest hotel prices of the year and first mountain flowers blooming. Drawbacks: some trails still closed, occasional Tianmen cable car shutdowns on windy days.

title: 10 life hacks for Zhangjiajie from veterans
text: Tips that save money, time and nerves: buy water outside the park (2 vs 10 yuan), install offline Maps.me, wear a red jacket for best photos, bring a thermos - free hot water stations inside, zip-lock bags for electronics, and buy souvenirs on the last day after knowing real prices.

title: History of Zhangjiajie - from village to fame
text: Known only to local Tujia and Miao until 1979, when artist Wu Guanzhong's paintings introduced the mountains to China. Became the first national forest park in 1982, UNESCO World Heritage in 1992, Avatar fame in 2009 and renamed Avatar Hallelujah Mountain in 2010.

title: Animals of Zhangjiajie - who you might see
text: The park shelters 150+ vertebrate species. You will definitely see the cheeky rhesus macaques along Golden Whip Stream. Likely spots: red-billed blue magpies, white egrets, giant butterflies. Lucky sightings: golden pheasants, giant salamanders (up to 1.5 m) and pangolins.

title: Plants of Zhangjiajie - what grows here
text: The park hosts over 3,000 plant species. The famous pines on the pillar summits are Chinese white pines (Pinus armandii), with roots that tap moisture from cracks in the quartzite. Seasonal colors: spring rhododendrons, summer emerald, autumn maples and ginkgos, winter snow on pines.
